title: 2. Reading order and sections: a few areas, then deeper

sections.name: summary
sections.label: In short
sections.content: The root lists a few purpose-shaped areas in reading order; each anchors a section that goes one level deeper.

sections.name: body
sections.label: The evidence
sections.content: The owner, 2026-10-27: "Navigation is a semantic essential" (baee7d9a). Decided: the root container's entry order is the navigation order, and a section root links to its section container (RFC-043 Changes E and F). Practised: srs-context's numbered layers, the muSrs regrouping into five areas (uncommitted), domain containers with the domain as identity (decision a6280447), and LiveWyer's ranked root. Not yet honoured by tools: navigation returns children out of order (srs-rust#1490), and srs-web's container pane shows search hits (srs-web#668). SP-83 (navigation unusable in a large repository) and SP-118 (nobody can say what the navigation is meant to be) stand. The topic thread on navigability (2bf30967) holds the owner's 2026-10-27 discussion.

sections.name: principle
sections.label: Principle
sections.content: The root's order is the reading order; every root member anchors a section; depth comes from the outline. Decided (RFC-043), practised, not yet honoured by tools; in tension with decision 0750c62f, which gives navigation depth to the contains tree.
